Ireland players again wore black armbands and bowed their heads during the Israeli national anthem to protest Israel’s actions in Gaza before the teams drew 1-1 in its bad-tempered second Nations League match on Sunday.
The Israeli players also wore black armbands in memory of the people killed in the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on October 7, 2023. Israel captain Dor Peretz had “7.10” written on his armband.
Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhín Kelleher stepped in as captain for Dara O’Shea – who was excused to be with his wife for the birth of their child – and he pointedly avoided shaking hands with Peretz, despite completing the usual pre-match formality with the referee and one of his assistants.
Kelleher repeated O’Shea’s actions before the first match in Debrecen, Hungary last week, when O’Shea avoided shaking Israel captain Manor Solomon’s hand. Ireland went on to win that game 3-0 through three first-half goals.
Solomon was dropped to the bench for Sunday’s match in Backa Topola, Serbia. Israel forward Sayed Abu Farchi was back in the squad after serving a suspension for getting sent off following his goal celebration during Israel’s 3-1 defeat to Austria on September 25. He didn’t play.
Finn Azaz, whose mother has Israeli heritage, also didn’t play and remained among the Irish substitutes.

Troy Parrott’s penalty in the 39th minute, after a foul by Peretz on Jimmy Dunne, gave Ireland a 1-0 halftime lead. A disagreement broke out on the sideline as the players made their way off the field.
Peretz lifted the back of his jersey above his neck before the second half started, seemingly to emphasise its Israel flag, and he equalised from close range two minutes after play resumed.
Substitute Omri Gandelman and Oscar Gloukh both hit the right post for Israel in the second half, when referee Juan Martínez Munuera was alert to tempers boiling over after some strong challenges.
Sunday’s game was initially supposed to be played in Dublin, but the Football Association of Ireland moved the game to a neutral venue for “operational reasons” in June following widespread calls for a boycott. The FAI said the game would be played with no fans present.
It followed the FAI’s own motion the previous November calling on UEFA to ban Israel from club and international competitions.
All the Irish players had been under pressure from home — where affinity with Palestinians is strong — to boycott the second match against Israel, though they faced the greatest pressure before the first game.
“I felt that pressure growing day by day and it’s getting almost to a breaking limit now,” Ireland coach Heimir Hallgrimsson said at the time.
Ultimately, only reserve goalkeeper Gavin Bazuno decided to skip both of the contentious games, saying in a statement that it was his “personal belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong.”
More than 160 Irish sportspeople had signed an open letter urging the FAI to reconsider its decision to go ahead with the two games.
Before the departure for Hungary, there were protesters outside the team hotel in Dublin calling on the players to boycott the matches. The SIPTU trade union displayed a huge poster in central Dublin beside the River Liffey asking the players to “Go with your conscience!” and “Don’t play with genocide” beside an image of a blood-splattered ball.
Former Ireland coach Brian Kerr said the FAI had “lost the respect of the Irish people” for going ahead with the games.
But the FAI resisted the calls, arguing the team could be hit with punishing sanctions by UEFA. Ireland is co-hosting the 2028 European Championship with England, Wales and Scotland.
Protesters threw tennis balls with Palestinian flags onto the field during Ireland’s 2-2 draw with Austria on Thursday, when a man with a Palestinian flag also later tried running onto the field.
On Saturday, an Israeli journalist stated during the pre-match press conference that the Irish players had called the Israeli players “monkeys” during last week’s game, leading to an immediate rebuke from Irish communications officer Kieran Crowley, who said it was “a lie” and ended the press conference.
The players had only decided to go ahead with the fixtures after a dramatic day in Debrecen before the first match, when both press conference and training were delayed for hours while they deliberated. They reportedly voted 14-8 in favor of continuing after Bazunu’s withdrawal that morning.
Ireland’s national broadcaster RTÉ was only providing stripped-back coverage of both games vs. Israel to meet contractual obligations. There was no studio presentation, commentary on the international feed, or analysis. RTÉ said it was not accepting advertising or sponsorship around either game.
RTÉ also announced recently that Ireland will boycott the Eurovision Song Contest for a second year over Israel’s participation.

A residential apartment is based on a simple idea: The people living there are known, visitors can be identified and the security staff is able to distinguish residents from outsiders.
Airbnb listings raise concerns over outsiders
Short-term rentals are rewriting that equation. What was once a home for a family or a long-term tenant can now effectively function as a hotel room, with a new guest arriving every few days, every night or even hourly basis.
India’s short-stay rules remain fragmented
The issue has been highlighted after a 28-year-old Gurgaon software engineer jumped off the 41st floor of an 
Airbnb
 apartment in Noida’s Supernova complex, though police said the incident had nothing to do with the rental. The man had checked into the apartment alone at around 3pm Friday and remained there for a day.
Debate grows over residential property use
The problem for housing societies is not who has booked a room, but how often unknown people enter a residential society. The issue had become controversial at Supernova even before the death. The apartment owners’ association recently issued a warning to owners and tenants not to list flats on Airbnb, Oyo and Booking.com for short stays citing security concerns and complaints about guests coming and going at odd hours.
The complex consists of three towers, with 582 residential units in Nova East and Nova West combined, while some 200 flats in Spira Tower between floors 19 and 43 are used for commercial purposes, the association said. All three towers have common gates and the same campus, and the movement of short-stay guests is a security concern for residents across the complex.
Verifying residents
For a normal tenant, societies generally get more time to get the police verification done, get the documents in place and find out who is staying in the flat. That process is greatly shortened by short term accommodation. A guest may come late at night, stay for one or two days and leave before neighbors or security guards get to know him.
This creates a different operating environment for a residential complex security personnel deal with frequent check-ins, delivery agents, visitors and vehicles, while residents have little idea who is temporarily using the apartments around them. Supernova was also concerned after a short-stay operator allegedly ran a security barrier when guards tried to stop him from entering through the main gate. Police later found six pending e-challans of around Rs 36,000 linked to the vehicle.
Residential-society rulebook
The bigger issue is that India's rules for this fast-growing accommodation model are still fragmented. Not all Airbnbs or short-term rentals are automatically illegal. It is contingent upon state tourism policies, local regulations, sanctioned land use, property documents and the bye-laws of the housing society.
The Union tourism ministry said in December 2025 that a report on homestays by the NITI Aayog had recommended states and Union Territories (UTs) to adopt best practices and harmonize regulations. Over 2000 registrations have already been done under Uttar Pradesh’s 2025 Bed and Breakfast and Homestay Policy, with about 750 certified by February 2026. The policy permits registered homestays in urban or rural areas, with a maximum of six rooms and 12 beds, provided the owner lives on the premises, among other conditions.
The battle is spreading across cities now
The friction is not restricted to Noida. Residents of Windsor Park in Vaibhav Khand, Ghaziabad, have raised concerns over alleged daily rentals, movement of outsiders and police verification. Residents of Bengaluru have also raised objections on the grounds of noise, parking and increased movement of outsiders to commercial activities in the form of homestays in residential neighborhoods.
The legal battle has now moved to the courts of Mumbai. A cooperative court upheld restrictions imposed by a housing society on short-term accommodation, saying the activity was commercial in nature and different from normal long-term renting. The ruling did not ban Airbnb use across the country but reiterated the “importance of society bye-laws and local laws and regulations”.
When does a house stop being a home?
That is the defining question for India’s high-rise societies today. Short-term rentals provide a way for homeowners to monetize an expensive asset and cash in on the growing demand for flexible accommodation. However, for residents, the same apartment can be a source of uncertainty since the occupants are constantly changing. The discussion is therefore moving away from whether an owner should be permitted to profit from a property. It’s about whether a residential building can be used at the same time as a home for permanent residents and a hotel-like property for transient guests — without changing the security, privacy and character of the entire community.

Capital punishment only possible if reformation of convict is ruled out: Supreme Court
The bench criticised the trial court for imposing the death sentence on the same day as conviction without a separate hearing on punishment.
The death penalty can be imposed only in cases where the possibility of a convict’s reformation is completely ruled out, the Supreme Court has held, underlining that the possibility of reform cannot be presumed absent merely because a crime is exceptionally brutal or grotesque.
SC sets strict threshold for imposing death penalty
According to a bench of justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Vijay Bishnoi, the prosecution must establish that life imprisonment is unquestionably inadequate as an alternative to capital punishment, and that the death sentence must be reserved for cases where the alternative of imprisonment for life is demonstrably foreclosed.
The ruling highlighted the distinction between the gravity of a crime and the separate question of whether the person who committed it is beyond reform — a distinction the law requires courts to examine before taking away a life.
Also read: Retired civic employee sentenced to life imprisonment for sexually assaulting minor relative
Court commutes death sentence in child rape-murder case
Applying this principle, the bench commuted the death sentence of a man convicted of repeatedly sexually assaulting his six-year-old stepdaughter and murdering her in 2018. The court, however, directed that he remain in prison for the remainder of his natural life, without the possibility of remission, holding that this was an appropriate punishment given the gravity of the crime.
In the present case, it said, the prosecution had failed to establish that the convict was beyond reform, while the material on his background and conduct in custody weighed against such a conclusion.
“The State has not excluded the possibility of the appellant’s reformation,” held the bench, adding that the alternative of imprisonment for the remainder of his natural life was adequate for a crime of such gravity.
The judgment emphasised that the sentencing exercise must consider the circumstances of the offender alongside those of the crime, rather than allow the enormity of the offence to eclipse every mitigating factor. The court said the death penalty was justified only when life imprisonment was “unquestionably foreclosed”.
Also read: Lucknow Pocso court gives man life term for abducting, sexually assaulting, killing 5-year-old boy
Court weighs crime’s brutality against mitigating factors
The bench did not minimise the brutality of the crime. The convict had repeatedly sexually assaulted the child, his stepdaughter, and killed her in April 2018, apparently to prevent her from disclosing the abuse. Her mother was the prosecution’s solitary eyewitness to the events inside the home.
Describing the killing as an instance of “instrumental silencing”, the court said the murder compounded the sexual violation of the child with an assault on the administration of justice. It called this an aggravating circumstance of the highest order, but stressed that even such gravity did not, by itself, establish that the offender was beyond redemption.
The court considered several mitigating circumstances, including the convict’s account of childhood deprivation and adult misfortune, the absence of previous criminal convictions, satisfactory conduct in custody, continuing family ties, his age of about 56 years and the nearly eight years he had spent in prison, including around seven under the shadow of a death sentence.
Also read: Goa govt moves Supreme Court, seeks life imprisonment for Tarun Tejpal in 2013 rape case
Trial court faulted over same-day sentencing
The psychological evaluation did not disclose any condition from which incorrigibility could be inferred. The state, meanwhile, had produced no evidence establishing that the possibility of reform could be ruled out. The court said these circumstances deserved genuine and substantial weight in deciding whether the ultimate punishment was warranted. The judgment also criticised the trial court for convicting and sentencing the accused to death on the same day, without a separate, meaningful hearing on sentence as required by law. The Supreme Court subsequently obtained additional material concerning his social and psychological background and prison conduct to ensure that the sentencing decision rested on a complete record.
At the same time, the bench ruled out ordinary life imprisonment carrying the prospect of remission after 14 years as inadequate for the crime. It invoked the intermediate sentencing option recognised in Union of India Vs V Sriharan (2016), under which a court can direct imprisonment for the convict’s entire natural life without remission.
Also read: Special court sentences 35-year-old man to life imprisonment in minor’s rape case
The death sentences for murder and aggravated penetrative sexual assault were accordingly commuted to imprisonment for the remainder of the convict’s natural life, without remission. The sentences for the other offences were upheld and ordered to run concurrently.
The court described the substituted punishment as one of the utmost severity, second only to death. It would ensure that the convict remained behind bars for the rest of his life, it said, while preserving the possibility of reformation that an irreversible death sentence would extinguish.

The Latest: Brazilians vote in presidential election dominated by Lula and Bolsonaro
Brazilians are voting in a pivotal presidential election featuring incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro
Brazilians are voting Sunday in a pivotal presidential election dominated by incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and his ideological opposite, Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro.
Preelection polls suggested both have a chance of winning outright, but if neither gets a majority of the vote, a runoff will be held on Oct. 25.
Nearly 159 million Brazilians are eligible to vote in Latin America’s largest economy. Bolsonaro is an ally of U.S. President Donald Trump and the son of ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro, whom Lula defeated four years ago.
Here's the latest:
The winner will lead a country that contains about 60% of the world’s largest rainforest — an ecosystem vital to the global climate.
But conservation of the Amazon has been largely absent from the presidential campaign.
Still, Lula and Bolsonaro represent starkly different visions of how the rainforest should be managed. Climate and conservation experts warn that a Bolsonaro victory could reverse the deforestation-control policies Lula restored after taking office in 2023.
During Jair Bolsonaro’s presidency, from 2019 to 2022, Amazon deforestation surged by about 60%, according to official data. Under Lula, deforestation has reached its lowest level in more than a decade.
Flávio Bolsonaro has pledged to end illegal deforestation by 2029. Lula proposes zero net deforestation by 2030, meaning any forest loss, legal or illegal, would have to be offset through restoration.
For many river dwellers, participating in the democratic process involves long journeys across the Rio Negro.
In Catalão, a floating community in the municipality of Iranduba just across from Manaus, residents arrived by boat to cast their ballots at the floating Nossa Senhora Aparecida municipal school.
Fisherwoman Francisca Oliveira Pontes traveled nearly an hour to reach the floating polling station. “My goal is to have a better country, and to exercise my right, which is the right to vote,” the 31-year-old Pontes said.
The vote center serves as a crucial hub for scattered Amazonian settlements, drawing voters from communities across the region, including Cacau Pirera and Careiro da Várzea.
Lula is watching the count with First Lady Rosângela da Silva at his residence in Sao Paulo’s upscale Alto de Pinheiros neighborhood, and then plans to head to a hotel downtown to speak to journalists.
Flávio Bolsonaro is watching with his family in his house in the capital of Brasilia.
Bolsonaro’s father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, cannot host his son in his residence in the same city because he is serving his 27-year prison sentence for an attempted coup.
Brazilian voters expressed confidence and pride in Brazil’s speedy electronic voting system as they cast their votes in downtown Rio de Janeiro, near a market teeming with fresh fruit and vegetables and a colonial-style church perched on a hill.
Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer, said that the rapid availability of results helped combat fraud and uncertainty.
“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” he said.
Fraud used to be a problem, but is no longer, said Tones José, 42, who works as a doorman. “Things have changed a lot since then. Now the urns are fully trustworthy.”
Failing to cast a ballot in Brazil's election incurs a small fine. Those who are illiterate, above the age of 70, and between 16 and 18 years of age may choose whether to exercise their right.
For Brazilians abroad, voting is required only in the presidential race.
Brazilian ex-President Jair Bolsonaro’s wife, Michelle Bolsonaro, is running for Senate in the Federal District, home to the capital, Brasilia.
A devout evangelical, the 44-year-old has never previously held public office.
In June, Michelle Bolsonaro had a very public falling out with Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, her stepson, whom she accused of disrespecting her in lengthy videos posted on her social media. The pair later made up.
She has called her candidacy “a mission” entrusted by her husband, who is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest following his conviction for an attempted coup.
Brazilians faced a long line to cast their vote in Paris, but morale was high and the atmosphere festive, with some singing and dancing to forró, a Brazilian style of music, and munching on coxinhas — an iconic, deep-fried savory snack.
Pablo José Feitosa Martins, a 48-year-old truck driver, was in line for an hour and a half to cast his vote. He moved to France in 2002 but grew up in the northeastern state of Pernambuco, as did President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
Feitosa Martins said that the incumbent had his vote because his social and industrial policies had transformed his region.
“There was a huge difference with the southeast,” he said by phone, referencing Brazil’s richer southern region where Sao Paulo and Rio are located. “There was nothing in the northeast, but now there is energy and water in the countryside, and people are no longer dying of hunger.”
In the last presidential election in 2022, women played a decisive role in handing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva a narrow victory over Flávio Bolsonaro’s father, former President Jair Bolsonaro.
In the lead-up to Sunday’s vote, candidates courted women with proposals to combat gender-based violence, a major campaign issue as violence against women reaches record levels and several high-profile cases draw attention.
Aware of women’s electoral weight, activists sought to leverage that power to seek guarantees that such promises won't later be shelved.
In cities across Brazil, Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro’s supporters wore the yellow and green of the Brazilian flag.
President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's supporters wore red T-shirts, some with the face of the young Lula in his union days and messages denouncing U.S. influence in Brazilian politics.
International election observers monitored the voting centers, where there was a usual security presence.
In one voting center in Sao Paulo, the energy was more subdued than four years ago, when Lula beat the senator’s father, former President Jair Bolsonaro.
“There’s definitely much less of an election vibe now,” said Celso Gaspar, 67, a retired teacher, who didn’t disclose who he voted for.
“Most people here feel they have a civic duty to fill, but there’s not that much passion for any candidate. A runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro can change that.”
Maria Ribeiro, a 50-year-old cellphone vendor from Brasilia, said that she voted for Flávio Bolsonaro to become Brazil's president because she wants freedom to express her evangelical religion.
She hopes that Bolsonaro follows in the footsteps of his father, Jair Bolsonaro.
“I voted for his father, and I don’t regret it,” she said, donning a yellow and green Brazil shirt at the voting center.
Rosangela Resende da Rocha, a 69-year-old who was previously a stay-at-home mom, said that she supported Lula’s social policies that help the “less fortunate” and how he stands up to U.S. President Donald Trump.
“That crazy guy wants to come in here to buy our country, so that our country will be like it is over there,” she said at a voting center in Brasilia. “He won’t succeed if Lula wins.”
“Win or lose, we are for Lula.”
Brazilians lined up to vote in Portugal’s capital like those living outside Brazil around the globe.
Some of those waiting to vote in Lisbon showed their Brazilian pride — one wearing a yellow and green Brazil soccer jersey, another a T-shirt with incumbent President Lula’s face emblazoned on the front.
“I will have dual nationality, but I’m still patriotic,” said Michele Sacramento, who’s lived in Portugal for seven years. “I love my country and I hope I can return one day and be able to walk in the street like I walk here, without any fear, any worry.”
Many are casting their ballots under the shadow of rising crime. Fears are most acute in Bahia, the country’s most violent state, a stronghold for President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
They are also high in Rio de Janeiro, Flávio Bolsonaro’s home state, where entrenched criminal factions and urban warfare have plagued communities for decades. Voters head to the polls demanding decisive federal action in the near future.
Brazil’s incumbent president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, voted after 9 a.m. in a school in Sao Bernardo do Campo, outside Sao Paulo.
The 80-year-old Lula said that he was confident that he could get his first outright victory in seven runs for the presidency. He also urged Brazilians above age 70, who aren’t legally required to vote, to show up and cast their ballots.
Wearing a hat to protect his head after a skin cancer diagnosis, Lula told journalists that he needs “to do double what we have done” if reelected and also said that “Brazil will not go forward by making arms sales easier,” in reference to a long-standing pledge of his main opponent, Flávio Bolsonaro.
Rosane Wink, 67, a retired engineer with German origins who voted in the same school as Flávio Bolsonaro, is a lifelong conservative voter who supports the former president’s son and his promise to classify criminal groups as terrorist organizations.
“It’s a kind of terrorism that they’re doing with us,” said Wink, who was wearing a T-shirt with Brazil’s national colors.
Last month, a robber held a gun to her stomach and then bit her hand and removed her wedding ring, she said.
“We’re not going to succeed in putting an end to crime, but we have to find a way to diminish it.”
Brazil's patron saint is Our Lady of Aparecida.
A comment on Jesus by Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro recently went viral, triggering fears among many Catholics that he might intend to remove the patron saint status of Our Lady of Aparecida — a claim Bolsonaro has denied.
In an Aug. 23 video, Bolsonaro said that he would “declare that Brazil belongs to the Lord Jesus Christ.” Some Catholics interpreted that as meaning that the presidential candidate would remove Our Lady of Aparecida as Brazil’s patron saint.
Our Lady of Aparecida is a much-beloved figure among Brazilians. The accusation tapped into Catholics’ fears over losing ground to evangelicals and could weaken the presidential bid of Bolsonaro, who is evangelical.
Bolsonaro has no authority to name or remove patron saints. That’s entirely up to the Vatican.
Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro has voted in his home state of Rio de Janeiro.
“Brazil needs change, Brazil can’t stand so much suffering,” said Bolsonaro, who arrived at around 8:10 a.m. local time to vote in a school.
He was dressed in a light yellow shirt featuring a “22” sticker, corresponding to the number that Brazilians must punch into electronic voting machines if voting for him.
“I am more than prepared to preside this country to give back to Brazilians the right to dream,” he told journalists.
President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's government sees a series of recent U.S. measures — including tariffs and the decision to classify Brazil’s biggest drug-trafficking groups as foreign terrorist organizations — as attempts to tip the scale in Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro’s favor, an accusation that the Trump administration has denied.
A victory by Bolsonaro would mean Brazil would join Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica and Peru in electing Trump-friendly governments in recent years.
Lula has made Brazil’s sovereignty a major campaign issue. In the days before the election, his team launched a Portuguese version of the Bad Bunny song, “Lo que le paso a Hawaii,” that uses the U.S. colonization of Hawaii as a cautionary tale.
Brazilian voters prepare number-heavy lists to remember their candidates’ numbers and at the ballot box, punch in the corresponding digits. Brazilian authorities adopted electronic voting machines in the 1990s to tackle longstanding fraud.
In earlier elections, ballot boxes were stuffed or stolen, and individual votes were routinely falsified, according to Brazil’s electoral authority. Now, results are reported mere hours after polls close.
In the lead-up to the 2022 vote, Jair Bolsonaro repeatedly cast unfounded doubts on Brazil’s electronic voting system. No significant fraud has ever been detected.
Alongside regional heavyweights like U.S. President Donald Trump and Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega, 80-year-old Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stands among the oldest leaders in the Americas.
If Lula achieves an outright victory against 45-year-old Flávio Bolsonaro, he will cement a historic milestone, becoming the oldest man ever elected to lead the South American nation.
He says he wants to live to be 120. He tried to ease concerns by posting workout videos to attempt to convince voters that age is just a number.

Almost 159 million Brazilians are eligible to vote in this tense political showdown.
Brazilians will also elect 27 state governors, members of state legislatures, all 513 federal members of the lower house of congress and 54 of the country’s 81 senators in Sunday’s vote.

Many local restaurants and delis will offer gift cards or picnic baskets, so it's worth checking if your giftee has a favorite.
- Milk Bar gift cards open up a world of delectable desserts, from cakes and pies to cookies and truffles.
- Omaha Steaks offers gift cards so folks can order their preferred cuts, from ribeyes to filet mignons, plus burgers and franks, seafood, chicken, desserts, and more.
- Goldbelly gift cards let you order culinary delights from across the US. If your giftee complains they can no longer get their favorite cakes, sandwiches, or fried chicken because they moved out of state, there’s a good chance they’ll be able to find it, or something similarly great, from a small restaurant or shop on Goldbelly.
- OpenTable offers gift cards for restaurants in various locations, making it easy to find top-rated eating spots near your giftee and set them up with a tasty treat.
- GrubHub gift cards let family and friends order in from their favorite restaurants. They simply enter their address to see a list of nearby restaurants that offer delivery or takeout.
- HelloFresh gift cards allow your recipient to try HelloFresh meal kits or sign up for a meal plan. (Use our HelloFresh promo codes for extra savings on gifts.)
- DoorDash gift cards can be used to order directly to your door from countless restaurants, convenience stores, and grocery stores.
Movie and TV Subscriptions
We are living in a golden age of entertainment. It has never been easier to get great TV and film pumped into your home. Cord-cutting gives us more control, and there’s an increasingly wide choice of streaming services you can give as presents.
- Netflix Gift Cards at Target and Amazon: The streaming pioneer boasts an impressive library of TV shows and movies, including exclusives like Wednesday, Stranger Things, and Squid Game. To ditch ads and stream in 4K on up to four devices at once, the price jumps from $9 to $27 per month.
- Paramount+ Gift Cards at Amazon and Best Buy: The home of Star Trek has a growing roster of shows and some good movies. A few other streaming services are also worth gifting.
- Sling TV for Live and Local TV: This app works on phones, PCs, or a streaming device like Roku and offers live TV channels, like a cable subscription, but over the internet. It’s one of the most affordable livestreaming services and lets you choose between channel bundles. Live TV is ideal for folks who love sports and talk shows.
- Disney+ Gift Cards at Walmart: This makes a thoughtful gift for those with young kids, though many adults will also enjoy a dose of nostalgia with classic Disney movies and shows, plus The Simpsons, Star Wars, Marvel, Pixar, NatGeo, and more.
- Hulu gift cards are ideal for cord-cutters who want a mix of on-demand TV shows and movies, with an optional live TV component.
- Mubi: With its handpicked selection of international arthouse films, fans of cinema seeking obscure indies and influential classics will love this subscription. You can also get a year for $120.
Music Streaming Services
Music makes a wonderful gift. It can conjure memories, boost your mood, and get you dancing. Our Best Music Streaming Services guide runs through our favorites and why we like them in more detail, but these subscriptions are the best options for most people. (Spotify, one of our top picks, no longer offers gift cards.)
- Apple Gift Card for Apple Music ($12 per month): It boasts millions of lossless tracks, and the mobile apps are solid.
- Google Play Gift Cards for YouTube Music ($12 per month): YouTube Music offers a huge library and starts at $12 per month, but if you watch a lot of YouTube videos, YouTube Premium costs $16 a month and offers an ad-free experience.
- Tidal Gift Card ($12 per month): Audiophiles will appreciate the streaming quality here, and Tidal boasts more than 100 million songs.
Ebooks and Audiobooks
There’s nothing quite like settling down with a good book, whether you read it on a Kindle, tablet, or smartphone. Ebooks and ebook subscriptions make great gifts, and many fantastic audiobook versions feature big-name casts for folks who love to listen. Amazon dominates this scene, but it’s not the only game in town.
- Amazon Kindle Unlimited ($12 per month): This lets anyone who reads on a Kindle or a device with the Kindle app borrow up to 20 books at a time from a library of millions. There are discounts for longer gift subscriptions (6, 12, or 24 months).
- Libro.fm (2-credit bundle for $30): This audiobook service supports local booksellers (you can pick a store) and splits the profit from your purchases. Plus, it boasts expert curation from booksellers.
- Audible Plus ($45 for 3 months): You get one free book to download per month, and access to a bunch of included Amazon audiobooks, including many bestsellers. You can also gift individual ebooks or audiobooks by selecting the “Give as a Gift” option on Amazon.
- Epic! ($40 for 3 months): This digital reading platform for kids 12 and under has more than 40,000 titles and includes audiobooks, interactive videos, quizzes, tracking tools, badges, and rewards to encourage reading, as well as personalized recommendations.
Digital News and Magazines
Some of the best journalism you can find online requires a subscription. Magazine, journal, and newspaper subscriptions make great gifts for anyone.
- WIRED is just $24 for a year of unlimited online access, though there's a higher tier if you want the print edition. If we may be so bold, it’s ideal for any tech lover in your life.
- The New Yorker has a digital-only subscription for $52 per year that includes new articles, access to the archive, and crossword puzzles.
- The New York Times is $75 for a year, which nets your giftee unlimited articles, podcasts, and videos via the website or app.
- The Atlantic costs $90 per year for a digital subscription and offers an array of well-reported stories and newsletters.
- MAD Magazine is $20 for six issues a year, and a subscription is now the only way to get this legendary (and damn funny) magazine outside of comic shops.
- ProPublica is a nonprofit that runs off donations. You don't need to subscribe to read top-notch unbiased reporting, but you can contribute to this Pulitzer-winning news organization in someone's name.
Gaming Subscriptions
There may be too many gaming subscription services now, but that’s good news for gift shoppers with gamers on their list.
- Xbox Game Pass Ultimate ($69 for 3 months) was the best deal in gaming until the price hike. It includes hundreds of titles, including frequent new releases, to download and play on Xbox or PC. It also includes access to the Xbox Cloud Gaming streaming service so you can play on even more devices.
- Nintendo Switch Online ($20 per year) is a must-have for online play and cloud game saving. It also gives access to classic NES and SNES games. If you opt to add the Expansion Pack, you’ll pay $50 for a year, but this adds N64 and Sega Genesis games as well as DLC for Animal Crossing.
- Humble Choice memberships cost $15 per month and give access to new mainstream and indie PC games every month, as well as a curated library. You can also gift Humble Bundles, and a portion of every purchase goes to charity.
- Apple Arcade for iPhone and iPad is $7 per month or $50 a year and has more than 200 games. Again, there’s no specific gifting option, but an Apple Gift Card can pay for an Apple Arcade subscription.
- PlayStation Plus Essential costs $11 per month or $80 per year. It's essential for anyone who wants to play online multiplayer on a PlayStation 5 or PS4, and it gives access to monthly free games. If they already have it, consider PlayStation Plus Extra ($17 per month or $135 per year) for a catalog of around 400 games, or PlayStation Plus Premium ($20 per month or $160 per year) for more than 700 games and cloud streaming access.
- Google Play Pass for Android phones costs $5 per month or $30 a year and provides access to a library of ad-free games and apps for Android phones and tablets. You can’t gift the subscription specifically, but you can send a Google Play gift code for someone to spend on Play Pass.
- Steam PC game store gift cards come in various sizes and make great gifts for PC gamers. Steam has a library of more than 50,000 games.
- Roblox gift cards can be redeemed for Robux (Roblox’s digital currency) in this popular free gaming platform.
- Twitch gift cards can be used to subscribe to your giftee's favorite online streamers.
Password Managers and Security
If you have family or friends with questionable online security habits, no amount of nagging will change their ways, but buy them a digital security gift, and they might just try it. Here are a few security-related digital gift ideas. (We also have more info in our Best Password Managers and Best VPNs guides.)
- 1Password starts at $3 per month if you pay annually, and gift cards are available in $25, $50, or $100 amounts. It’s one of our favorite password managers: it works on every platform, has tons of integrations and add-ons, and offers lots of useful extras, like travel mode.
- Malwarebytes Premium costs $40 per year and covers five devices. It goes way beyond your average antivirus program to guard against malware and other cyber threats, like phishing and malicious URLs. It’s easy to use, speedy, and less intrusive than a lot of popular antivirus software.
- NordVPN starts at $3 per month, but you can get deeper discounts for longer terms, such as $81 per year, or even cheaper if you catch one of its frequent discount deals. It’s one of our favorite virtual private networks, deservedly popular, and offers servers all around the world. It can stop people from snooping on you and help you bypass geographical restrictions on streaming services like Netflix.
Online Teaching Courses
Everyone wants to acquire new skills, but motivation can be hard to come by. If your loved ones talk about learning a musical instrument, a new language, or picking up some photography skills, why not spring for some online lessons to help them get started?
- MasterClass starts at $120 per year and offers classes on all sorts of topics from seriously big-name celebrities. You can sign up for cooking classes from Gordon Ramsay, storytelling tips from Neil Gaiman, film classes from David Lynch, songwriting help from Alicia Keys, or learn skateboarding from Tony Hawk.
- Rosetta Stone ($159 for a year) offers comprehensive language-learning courses. For total immersion, lessons are conducted in the target language and feature interactive real-life scenarios and pronunciation feedback. Check out our Best Language Learning Apps guide for more options.
- Lessonface gift cards start at $25. This online platform connects students of all ages and abilities with music teachers. Lots of reviews and filters help you find the right teacher. Online lesson rates vary, but you can buy gift cards starting at $25.
- Fender Play ($98 for 6 months) offers online lessons for guitar (acoustic, electric, or bass) and ukulele. The mobile app and online lessons are suitable for beginners or for intermediate guitarists looking to improve.
- Babbel starts at $81 for 6 months and gives access to all languages; it's our favorite language-learning app. With a focus on useful vocabulary, it teaches the basics of grammar before moving on to conversational scenarios in common settings.
- Preply, around $15 per 50-minute lesson, is perfect for anyone looking to get serious about learning a language. It connects you with tutors for online lessons, but prices vary.
- The School of Photography ($155 per year) has online courses, hundreds of videos, Lightroom presets, and monthly assignments. Any photographer, whether a hobbyist or pro, can develop their skills.
- CodeSpark Academy ($60 for 6 months) is a game-based app that teaches kids ages 5 to 10 the fundamentals of coding. It stars cute monsters and challenges kids to solve a series of puzzles. Everything is visual, so there’s no reading required. They can also make and share their own interactive stories and games.
Fitness Services
Staying fit is crucial for good health and overall well-being, and our favorite fitness apps and services can help anyone do it with online classes that guide workouts from home. Exercise some caution when gifting fitness services, though. Make sure your intended recipient is genuinely interested.
- ClassPass (from $19 per month) gives access to fitness studios and gyms, a wide variety of at-home workouts, and beauty and spa treatments. Basic membership gives you eight credits, enough to book up to two classes.
- Apple Fitness+ ($10 per month) is packed with slick video and audio workouts ranging from kickboxing to yoga. It’s a great choice for beginners, as workouts rarely require any equipment, are well explained by the charismatic instructors, and always include variations for folks at different levels. While you can’t give a subscription, an Apple Gift Card can be used for Fitness+ or any of Apple’s other services.
- Peloton ($13 per month) is a popular fitness brand that sells expensive exercise bikes and treadmills, but you can also get an app subscription that gives access to on-demand and live workouts that people can do with whatever equipment they have. There’s no direct way to gift a Peloton membership, but you can use an Apple or Google Play gift card on the app.
- Strava ($12 per month) is an excellent tracking and training app for runners and cyclists. There is a free tier, but the subscription allows for more in-depth analysis, custom goals, route planning, segment competition, personal heat maps, and more. You can't gift membership directly anymore, but you can use an Apple or Google Play gift card in the app.
Shopping Loyalty Programs
Some retail memberships or subscriptions give access to better deals, free priority shipping, and other benefits that make them highly appreciated gifts.
- Walmart+ membership ($98 per year): If you know a frequent Walmart shopper, this includes free shipping and grocery deliveries, discounts on fuel, pharmacy discounts in some states, and contactless checkout on a smartphone. You can't gift a membership anymore, but you can buy a gift card that folks can use to subscribe.
- Amazon Prime ($139 per year): You likely already know about this service, but these are the perks if you don't. It includes fast free shipping, video and music streaming, ebooks and games, and various exclusive deals and discounts. You can no longer buy Prime as a gift, but you can use an Amazon gift card to get it. It costs $15 per month if you don't pay annually.
- Costco’s Gold Star Membership ($65 per year): The recipient gets access to more than 700 Costco locations and the website, with frequent deals to be found on everything from big-ticket electronics to wholesale groceries.
Travel and Experiences
Many of us are getting back into the swing of traveling and are looking to make up for lost time, so why not give the gift of a trip?
- Uncommon Experiences offers interactive virtual classes covering cookery, cocktails, painting, songwriting, and many other activities. They send kits out before each class, but giftees may need to buy some of their own ingredients.
- Virgin Experience Gifts include driving experiences, active adventures, golfing trips, foodie tours, and a whole host of other options. You can search by location, so it is easy to check what's available near your recipient. You can buy eGift Cards in any amount.
- 57hours Gift Cards start at $100 and fund outdoor adventures with local guides worldwide. Categories include rock climbing, hiking, kiteboarding, surfing, mountain biking, and more. You can search by location and activity, but some places have more options than others, and trips can get pricey.
- StubHub Gift Cards from $25 can be used for sports games, concerts, theater, and other live events across the US.
- The Metropolitan Museum of Art Gift Membership from $120 gives your recipient and a guest free admission to New York's most popular museum, with five preview days for access to exhibitions before they open to the public, members-only tours, and more.
- Spafinder Gift Cards from $50 can be used in spas and salons near you for mani-pedis, massages, haircuts, and even wellness retreat getaways.
- AMC Theatres Gift Cards start at $5 and can be used for movie tickets, popcorn, and other concession goodies.
- Airbnb Gift Cards start at $25, and you can also get physical cards from Amazon. You can use them for any stay or experience.
- A US Park Pass for $80 a year gives you access to more than 60 national parks, including Yosemite, Alcatraz Island, and the Everglades.
- Uber gift cards can be used for rides almost anywhere.
Donate to Charity in Their Name
Many of us have more than we need, and gifts can be hit or miss. Making a charitable donation in someone’s name is a great alternative that lets people know you’re thinking of them and also does some good in the world. Just be careful to do a little research on your chosen charity or service before you spend. Organizations like Charity Navigator and Charity Watch can help you find the most deserving and trustworthy charities.

These make great gifts for animal lovers and come with an optional soft toy and information pack. The WWF does have a large infrastructure to support, but it takes its mission to protect wildlife and the environment very seriously.

Prisons DIG Somashekar held over forged SC order used to free life convict in 2018
DIG M Somashekar was arrested for allegedly using a forged Supreme Court order to release a life convict in 2018. Police investigate the case.
Deputy Inspector General of Prisons (DIG) M Somashekar, who was the chief superintendent of Parappana Agrahara Central Prison in 2018, was arrested on Sunday night over the alleged use of a forged Supreme Court order to free a life convict from the jail that year.
Somashekar was produced before an ACMM court on Monday and remanded to five days in police custody, Parappana Agrahara police inspector Naveen Kumar said.
The investigation follows the release of S Shankar, who walked out of the prison on November 13, 2018, after officials received a document purportedly ordering his release from the Supreme Court.
Police are examining how the document was prepared, how it reached the prison and how it was processed and verified before Shankar was released. They are also examining Somashekar’s role as the prison’s chief superintendent at the time.
Shankar had been serving a life sentence in a murder and kidnapping for ransom case. He was arrested in 2001 and booked under sections 364A and 120B of the Indian Penal Code. He was later convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment, with the sentences directed to run concurrently.
The police have already arrested Shankar and S Srikanth, a former second division assistant at Parappana Agrahara Central Prison.
Investigators suspect Srikanth of preparing the forged Supreme Court document.
“The investigation has revealed that a fabricated document was presented as a Supreme Court order and that a life convict was released from prison in 2018 on that basis. Two persons have already been arrested in connection with the case, and we are also examining the role of the prison officials who were responsible at that time,” Kumar said.
Investigators are now tracing what happened between the preparation of the alleged fake order and Shankar’s release from prison.
“We are trying to establish how the fake order was prepared, how it reached the prison authorities and who all were involved in the process of releasing the convict. The relevant records and other evidence are being examined as part of the investigation,” Kumar said.
Somashekar is currently serving as DIG in the Prisons Department in Kalburgi.

Player welfare, injury worries & boredom - has extended break worked?
- Published
The first international break of the 2026-27 season is almost over - and it has been a longer one than fans are used to.
For the first time, the Premier League and Championship paused for three weeks rather than the usual two with players returning to domestic action from Friday.
The idea was brought in by Fifa with player welfare in mind, but, with a growing list of injuries, has it really been a success?
Who benefits from an extended international schedule? And do people really want a three-week break from domestic action when the season has only just got going?
Why was extended break brought in?
In recent years, Fifa has used five primary international breaks during the season, all consisting of two-week gaps in March, June, September, October and November.
The switch to a three-week gap across late September and early October, alongside reducing the number of breaks down to four, was made for a number of reasons.
One was that the scheduling of the 2026 World Cup final on 19 July was the latest date for a summer World Cup since 1966.
Player welfare also featured in the discussions, this including travel considerations.
The reduction in the number of breaks will reduce the number of journeys some players face in having to travel from one continent to another for their international fixtures . One such example is African and South American players who play their domestic football in Europe and have to travel cross-continent to fulfil international fixtures.
But with the domestic season just starting to get interesting, fans tend to bemoan the interruption - no matter the length - and long for the return of club football.
Injury nightmares
The extended international break might have been brought in with player welfare in mind, but the reality is that a number of players will return to their clubs with injuries.
It is hard to quantify whether more injuries have been picked up during the past fortnight than during other international breaks and it must be factored in that this is a lengthier break with more fixtures. A full and fair comparison might have to wait until the end of the season, after all the international breaks.
However, there have been numerous injuries to players since players joined up with international team-mates.
On Monday, it was announced that Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott had withdrawn from the England squad with a thigh injury and the Cherries are unhappy with the way they believe England handled the injury.
Manchester City striker Erling Haaland asked to be substituted on 67 minutes, subsequently limping off in Norway's match against Portugal on Sunday before leaving camp on Monday while club team-mate Nico O'Reilly returned to City for further assessment.
Following the injury to Haaland, the Norwegian players' union (NISO) expressed concern over the increased demands.
"Over time, we have seen a worrying trend where the burden on top players has become far too high," NISO chief Kristoffer Vatshaug said.
"We want clearer guidelines for workload and recovery. It is about the time between matches, consecutive rest periods, travel strain and how much time players get to recover after a long season."
Liverpool duo Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak have both picked up injuries with Gakpo withdrawing from the Netherlands squad with an ankle injury and Isak pulling out of Sweden duty with a minor thigh injury.
Portugal boss Jorge Jesus revealed Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes had been playing through pain while Sunderland's Dan Ballard and Brian Brobbey both sustained hamstring problems.
Club managers will have their fingers crossed that no more names are added to that list with three days of fixtures still to be played.
England's Tino Livramento, Kobbie Mainoo, Cole Palmer, Marcus Rashford and Declan Rice all pulled out of Thomas Tuchel's squad before the start of the break.
Away from the Premier League, there have also been injuries to some of the biggest stars in the game with Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe sustaining an injury while on duty with France and Barcelona's Raphinha also returned from Brazil with a thigh injury.
'More challenging' but 'positives to take' - Tuchel
England boss Thomas Tuchel has previously been critical of the three-week break, saying it is "more challenging" than previous years, citing travel and having only two days of rest between games as problems.
In a news conference on Monday before England take on the Czech Republic on Tuesday he said: "I can assure everyone that player welfare is priority number one.
"But new training styles and training times, different positions to play maybe, increase the chance of injury."
On whether the extended break has had an impact on injuries, he said "we need to get the numbers right" before deciding.
"Is it really more or is it the same amount [of games] as in two shorter little windows? I don't have the answer to that," he said.
"The two-week window is not guilty for everything. If it is a thing, we will adapt and make the most of it as always.
"I didn't like the start of it after a long tournament to have a long window. There are also positives to it like we saw against Croatia after having three matches together.
"The team is together for longer, more training sessions, more meetings, more of the same language. You see improvements and automatisms clicking in. We made it a very good camp."
What do fans say?
Shay, Swindon: I don't think any Premier League or Championship fan backs this idea. It's just boring without your club in action for so long.
James McCreadie: Fans are getting sick and tired of losing players to what is a glorified friendly. Teams in Europe and Carabao Cup have nine games in 28 days or so before the next international break. Hope clubs pull players out, citing that player welfare comes first.
Matt, York: The amount of injuries during this break, most of them muscular, including the usually extremely robust Erling Haaland surely highlights it has been a mistake of an experiment. Whoever thought it a good idea after a long World Cup summer needs to be in for a performance review.
Kelvin Thomas: Too many players are being withdrawn due to injuries. But I am sure they will make a miraculous recovery when back at there clubs. Even with them gone England will win (bring it on).
James: Revealing that players came to camp with minor issues highlights the pointed comments about Cole Palmer (and I'm sure others) who seem to value their club more than country. Last chance saloon for a few of them come next internationals.
It's not all negative though...
The international break signals an opportunity for fans to swap their usual Premier League or Championship ticket for a trip to a local lower league club or Women's Super League match.
Women's teams associated with a Premier League club often take the opportunity to play their home matches at the larger men's stadium to allow more fans to attend.
Without tiers one and two of the football pyramid in action, it also means room on the television schedule for lower-league matches - a financial boost for those clubs.
While it is difficult to compare week by week attendances because of the number of variables, the international break does offer some fans the chance to watch other teams in action.
Across the 11 games played in League One and League Two on Saturday – nine postponed because of international call-ups – only three had attendances less than their home average for the season.
In the WSL, five of the seven games played over the weekend had a higher attendance than the home club's season average.

India is likely to have a much older population later this century, as the country’s age structure is beginning to shift and fertility has fallen “below replacement,” Moody’s Ratings said on Tuesday (September 29, 2026).
Moody’s said population growth has long been a tailwind for economic growth and creditworthiness, but falling fertility is now changing that picture.
Fewer workers will limit productive capacity, while fewer households and consumers will weaken demand. As a result, countries will have to rely more on productivity to sustain growth.
Moody’s said the global fertility rate had declined from 4.9 children per woman in 1950 to about 2.2 today, only slightly above the replacement rate of 2.1.
“What makes this episode particularly significant is that many of the world’s largest economies are ageing at the same time. In fact, more than 70% of the world’s population now lives in countries with fertility rates at or below replacement level,” Moody’s said in a report on global demographics.
It said fertility rates across much of Latin America were now comparable to those of Europe and Japan, while several East Asian countries had some of the lowest fertility rates ever recorded.
Japan has the most top-heavy population structure, with nearly 30% of its population over 65 and about 11% under 15.
South Korea is close behind, while China is moving rapidly in the same direction. Emerging markets, including Brazil, India, Thailand and Türkiye, are also progressing along the same path.
“Although India’s population remains relatively young, fertility has already fallen below replacement and the country’s age structure is beginning to shift, setting the stage for a much older population later this century,” Moody’s said.
Declining fertility ultimately reshapes age structures as well as population growth, it said. Countries experiencing the steepest fertility declines today will also age most rapidly in the coming decades.

A heavy Monday morning rush brought traffic on the Chandapura stretch to a standstill for several hours, with vehicles returning to Bengaluru after the long weekend adding to the congestion. Office-goers said they were stuck from around 7 a.m., while some school students reached school nearly three hours late.
Many people who had travelled towards Hosur on Friday night for the long weekend began returning to Bengaluru on Monday morning as offices and schools reopened. This added to the usual morning rush on the already congested stretch.
Rajesh K., a resident of the area, said he left home at 7 a.m. expecting traffic but was still delayed by nearly two hours. “Even two-wheelers had no space to move,” he said.
Residents told The Hindu that the stretch has been seeing heavy traffic for some time due to ongoing road work and poor road conditions, which have slowed down traffic. The situation was worse on Monday morning, they said.
School students were also caught in the traffic, with some having examinations on Monday. Residents said school buses and vans were stuck for hours and could not take other routes. The traffic was further affected by the narrow stretch near the railway track, where police and civic workers were clearing stagnant rainwater. The work took up part of the already narrow road and added to the traffic.
Traffic police were deployed to regulate the movement of vehicles and clear the bottleneck. The police said it took more than two hours for traffic movement to return to normal.
A traffic police officer said the existing two-lane stretch near the railway track needs to be widened to four lanes to prevent traffic from building up. “Widening the road from two lanes to four lanes at the railway track would significantly ease traffic movement and prevent such bottlenecks,” the officer said.

In Summary
- Xiaomi released a number of power banks in the Indian market recently.
- The most eye-catching of the new power banks is the Xiaomi UltraThin Magnetic Power Bank, which is the successor to the Ultra Slim power bank launched last year.
- The UltraThin Magnetic Power Bank is the slimmest power bank in its class – it is a mere 6 mm thin, and less than 100 grams in weight. It also comes with a super premium design, with a metal build and a fiberglass wireless charging area.
- It has a premium design and feel, but the Xiaomi UltraThin Magnetic Power Bank comes with a stiff price tag of Rs 5,999, which many might find outrageous for a 5000 mAh power bank. But it could be perfect for many others!
Power banks and “beauty” are seldom used in the same sentence. They are notorious for being bulky, heavy, and brick-like. Even the ones that can be slapped on the back of your phone and attached magnetically often feel uncomfortable to use along with a smartphone. Unless one is using the Xiaomi UltraThin Magnetic Power Bank.
Xiaomi pleasantly surprised us all with a super thin power bank last year, the Xiaomi Ultra Slim power bank, which was so slim and compact that many of us had mistaken it for a card holder. It, however, lacked wireless charging, so it could not be stuck onto the back of a phone. The UltraThin power bank fixes this shortcoming. It comes with a 5,000 mAh battery with up to 15W wireless charging support, and 22.5W charging support (up from 20W on the Ultra Slim). While these numbers are nothing to rave about, it is the design and build of the power bank that are showstoppers. But can its lightweight make up for its rather heavy price tag of Rs. 5,999? Let’s find out:
Xiaomi UltraThin Magnetic Power Bank Design and Appearance: A treat to hold and carry!
It is difficult to think that anything out of the ordinary can be done with the design of power banks, given just how simple and functional the devices are, but Xiaomi has managed to make the design of the UltraThin power bank its biggest USP. As the name suggests, the power bank is truly “ultra thin.” In fact, at 6mm, it is almost half as thin as the Ultra Slim power bank that impressed us last year, and is the thinnest power bank we have used to date.
The power bank is quite compact as well. It is 98.5 mm tall, 71.5 mm wide, and weighs just 98 grams, which means that it will not only easily fit on the back of any phone out there, but will add only about as much weight as a routine phone case. Even though the Xiaomi UltraThin powerbank is quite sleek, it still feels very sturdy. The body is made of an aluminum alloy shell, giving it that reassuring solid feel, and the wireless charging side comes with fiberglass.
The power bank is available in three different colors – Graphite black, Glacier Silver, and Radiant Orange. While we received the black color option, we think all three colors look very good – the bright orange is the exact shade of the iPhone 17 Pro series’ orange and will basically blend with your iPhone 17 Pro or Pro Max (Apple seems to have stepped away from the shade in its latest iPhones, though).
Our unit came with a matte finish, and the back has a small “Mi” logo in a glossy contrast. The thin sides curve softly around the edges, while the front (which is the part that connects wirelessly to your phone) has a huge circular mark to highlight wireless charging connectivity, along with some information. All the sides are bare except the base, which has a small power button, a USB Type-C port for charging, and four tiny LED lights highlighting the amount of charge in the power bank.
The Xiaomi UltraThin Magnetic power bank is a treat to both hold and carry. It exudes premiumness, and its thin form factor makes it easy to carry around, regardless of whether you hold it in your hand, carry it in your trouser pocket, or in your bag. Or even on your phone. It was so thin and light that we actually used it as a bookmark from time to time.
Xiaomi UltraThin Magnetic Power Bank Specs and Hardware: Decent, rather than exceptional
The Xiaomi UltraThin Magnetic Power Bank is more about style and convenience than specs. It comes with decent enough specs, but nothing that will make people sit up in surprise. The power bank comes with a 5,000 mAh battery, which is a touch more than the UltraSlim, which had a 4900 mAh battery. Xiaomi has used an advanced silicon carbon battery instead of the usual lithium-ion one, which allows more mAhs to be packed in a much smaller form factor.
In terms of charging speed, the Xiaomi UltraThin Magnetic Power Bank offers up to 15W wireless charging support and 22.5W wired charging support (up from 20W on the UltraSlim). That sounds brisk enough, but this 15W wireless charging speed is only delivered with the Xiaomi 17 series. For other smartphones that come with wireless charging support, you will get 7.5W charging speed, including the iPhones (MagSafe is supported, but the charging speed remains slow).
Xiaomi has added a number of safety features in the power bank as well. The brand says there are ten layers of safety protection on the device, including foreign object detection, overcurrent, short circuits, overvoltage, overcharging, overdischarging, and over-discharging, amongst other safety features.
Xiaomi UltraThin Magnetic Power Bank Performance: Super convenient, but not super fast
The Xiaomi UltraThin Magnetic Power Bank’s spec sheet means that it cannot fully charge most modern smartphones from 0-100 percent – while it has a capacity of 5000 mAh, its rated capacity is lower (3000 mAh), as in most power banks. As a result, it was able to take our iPhone 17 (which comes with a 3692 mAh battery) from 20 percent to nearly full only once. And as its wireless charging speed for iPhones is fairly sluggish, it took comfortably over an hour. And it took even longer to charge our Pixel 10 Pro XL. That said, thanks to its slim size and light weight, you can just stick it to the back of your phone and forget it.
If you need relatively faster charging, you can connect your phone to the power bank with a Type-C cable and enjoy 22.5W wired charging speed, which is pretty much three times the 7.5W wireless charging speed with non-Xiaomi 17 series phones, and does get the phone charged much faster in comparison. However, if your phone comes with a relatively big battery (and many phones these days are comfortably above 5000 mAh), the power bank might only be able to get them up to 40 or 50 percent charged before needing charging assistance itself.
While you can use the power bank to charge two devices at once – wired and wirelessly – that compromises speed and its charging capacity a fair bit, as both get divided. The power bank also gets fairly warm while charging a phone wirelessly, which can make the temperature of the phone attached rise too. Our iPhone 17 often got very warm while charging.
The magnetic hold of the power bank is very strong. It latched on very easily to our iPhone and did not budge when we kept the pair of them in our pocket or bags, or even while using the phone. This is by far the most comfortable and convenient power bank to use with a phone – you hardly feel its weight.
Xiaomi UltraThin Magnetic Power Bank Review Verdict: Pricey, premium and a convenience contender
The Xiaomi UltraThin Magnetic Power Bank comes with a very steep price tag of Rs 5999. You can get power banks with way more mAh, more ports, and much faster charging speeds at a lower price from Xiaomi itself. Other brands also have their version of slim power banks at far lower prices – Boat has the Magnacharge at Rs 1,599 and URBN the One Premium MagSafe at Rs 1,999. However, none of them brings the sleek form factor and the premium build that the Xiaomi UltraThin Magnetic Power Bank offers, nor the long-term assurance that the brand offers. In fact, its only real competitor would perhaps be Samsung’s Galaxy Magnetic Wireless battery pack, which comes with a similar capacity and 15W wireless charging, but is bulkier and not exactly super affordable at about Rs 4,900.
If you are in the market for a power bank with more mAh in capacity and more Ws in charging speed, and what’s more, want both for a small price tag, the Xiaomi UltraThin Magnetic Power Bank is not for you. However, if you are someone who wants to invest in an ultra-portable, very premium power bank which can simply give your smartphone a power-packed nudge without adding too much bulk to your gadget life, or even to your device itself, the Xiaomi UltraThin Powerbank might be perfect for you. Yes, it is expensive, but it brings with it terrific design, ease of use, and convenience, which is likely to be coveted by many premium phone users, especially those who use iPhones and Pixels!
The Xiaomi UltraThin Magnetic Power Bank’s style is its substance. And it is substantially stylish. Yes, it does have a big price tag, but then, convenience can also be a powerful feature of a power bank.

- Premium metallic build
- Good magnetic connectivity

The story so far: India is working towards eliminating dog-mediated human rabies by 2030. Yet the country does not have a single, comprehensive national count of human rabies deaths. While the Health Ministry’s disease surveillance system recorded 54 deaths in 2024, an ICMR-led study estimates that 5,726 people die of rabies in India every year.
Is rabies a notifiable disease in India?
Rabies is not a notifiable disease nationwide. Unlike diseases for which there is a clearly established national notification mechanism covering every State and Union Territory, rabies notification has historically depended on State-level notification requirements and the disease surveillance system.
The National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) has been working to make human rabies a notifiable disease across the country. Communications have been sent to States to notify the disease under the relevant State legislation.
However, a disease being under surveillance does not necessarily mean that every case or death occurring in the country is automatically captured in one central database.
Rabies is a particularly difficult disease to count because a large proportion of deaths can occur outside the formal health system. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is almost invariably fatal, but patients may die at home or in facilities that do not routinely report the death through disease-surveillance channels.
How is a disease chosen for notification in India?
Disease notification is largely a public-health surveillance and State-level regulatory function, while the Union government maintains national surveillance systems such as the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP).
A disease is generally prioritised for notification or surveillance when it has significant public-health importance — for example, high mortality or morbidity, epidemic potential, rapid spread, risk of international transmission, emergence of a new pathogen, or where early detection can trigger effective control measures. India’s disease-prioritisation exercises have considered epidemiological, clinical, economic and public-health factors, with expert consultation.
Once a disease/condition is designated for surveillance, health facilities, laboratories and health workers report cases through the surveillance system. Under IDSP, reporting includes suspected (S), presumptive (P) and laboratory-confirmed (L) cases. Data move from reporting units to District and State Surveillance Units and ultimately to the Central Surveillance Unit at the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC).
A rising or unusual cluster triggers investigation by Rapid Response Teams, which can lead to laboratory confirmation, containment measures and further reporting.
The exact legal notification requirement can depend on the State/UT and the particular disease. Leprosy, for instance, was declared a notifiable disease nationally in 2025.
So, how many people die of rabies in India?
There are different answers, depending on what is being measured. The Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme/Integrated Health Information Platform (IDSP–IHIP) recorded 21 human rabies deaths in 2022, 50 in 2023 and 54 in 2024.
The Registrar General of India’s Medical Certification of Cause of Death (MCCD) system, meanwhile, recorded 66 medically certified rabies deaths in 2022 and 271 in 2023.
But neither set of numbers represents all rabies deaths in India. The MCCD figures are based on medically certified causes of death. The system does not cover every registered death in the country. At the national level, medically certified deaths accounted for only about 22% of registered deaths in both 2022 and 2023.
The IDSP–IHIP figures serve a different purpose. They are generated through disease surveillance and are intended to identify and track cases and deaths reported through the surveillance network.
This is why the figures cannot simply be added together or compared as if they were measuring the same thing. Then where does the figure of 5,726 deaths come from?
An ICMR-led study published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases estimated that India has about 5,726 human rabies deaths every year.
The researchers did not arrive at this number by counting death certificates or hospital records.
They conducted a large community-based survey involving 337,808 people in 78,807 households across 60 districts in 15 States. The study estimated that India sees about 9.1 million animal bites every year, including around 5.6 million dog bites.
The researchers then combined information from the community survey and laboratory data with a probability decision-tree model to estimate how many people bitten by animals would develop rabies and subsequently die.
The 5,726 figure is therefore a modelled estimate of annual mortality, rather than a tally of deaths reported to the government.
Why is the difference so large?
This is because each system is designed to capture its own unique data.
IDSP–IHIP is primarily a disease-surveillance system. It depends on cases and deaths being detected and reported through the health system and surveillance network.
MCCD records medically certified causes of death. It provides valuable information on the causes of deaths that are medically certified, but it does not cover every death.
The ICMR-led study, on the other hand, attempts to estimate the actual burden in the population, including deaths that may never enter either surveillance or medical-certification systems.
This means that a low number in a surveillance database does not necessarily mean that the disease burden is low.
In rabies, the problem is compounded by the nature of the disease itself. Patients may not reach a hospital after symptoms begin; some deaths occur at home; and the animal bite that initiated infection may have happened weeks or months earlier.
There is also a critical point between the animal bite and a possible rabies death: post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). If a person receives appropriate wound care, rabies vaccine and, where indicated, rabies immunoglobulin promptly after exposure, death can be prevented.
What happens to a case of a notifiable disease?
India’s disease surveillance system works through multiple levels.
At the frontline are healthcare facilities, laboratories and other reporting units. When a suspected, probable or confirmed case of a disease covered by surveillance is detected, information is reported through the appropriate surveillance mechanism.
The information moves through district and State surveillance structures and is consolidated nationally through the IDSP/IHIP platform. The purpose is not simply to count cases. Surveillance is intended to detect unusual increases, identify outbreaks, understand geographical patterns and enable public-health authorities to respond.
But notification depends on detection, diagnosis and reporting. A person who never reaches a reporting facility, a death that occurs outside a medical setting, or a case that is not recognised as rabies may not enter the surveillance database.
This is why notification should not be confused with a census of every person who has the disease.
Does that mean the 5,726 figure is the “real” number?
The 54 deaths recorded by IDSP–IHIP in 2024 tell us how many deaths were reported through that surveillance system.
The 5,726 estimate attempts to answer a different question: how many people may actually be dying of rabies each year, including deaths that are missed by routine systems.
The study itself is therefore important not because it replaces surveillance data, but because it draws attention to what routine surveillance may be missing.
A senior Health Ministry official has also pointed out that the two figures are generated through different methods and should not be treated as directly equivalent. Together, however, they point to a substantial gap between reported surveillance deaths and estimated mortality.
Why does this matter when India wants to eliminate rabies by 2030?
Reliable surveillance is essential to rabies elimination. India cannot determine whether it is moving towards elimination if it cannot accurately establish where human rabies deaths are occurring, where dog-mediated transmission continues and which populations are not receiving timely post-exposure care.
The ICMR-led study also found important gaps after animal bites. About one in five dog-bite victims had not received anti-rabies vaccine, while only 66.2% had received at least three doses. Among those who received only one dose, nearly half did not complete the vaccination course. Only about one in 10 eligible victims received passive immunisation.
The gaps are therefore not confined to counting deaths. They extend across the entire rabies-control chain — from preventing dog bites and vaccinating dogs to recognising exposures, completing human post-exposure prophylaxis and recording outcomes.
As medical scientist and former ICMR Director-General Nirmal Kumar Ganguly puts it, the absence of consolidated data remains a challenge for rabies elimination. Cases and deaths can occur in places where they are difficult to measure, making stronger surveillance, dog vaccination and timely human post-exposure treatment critical.
Rabies is almost entirely preventable, but once symptoms appear, it is almost invariably fatal. That makes every missed exposure, incomplete vaccination course and unrecorded death significant.
For India, therefore, the question is not simply why one database reports 54 deaths while a study estimates 5,726.
The larger question is how many deaths the health system is failing to see — and whether India can close that surveillance gap before it attempts to declare dog-mediated human rabies eliminated by 2030.
